health-clubs.headline: Genesis Health Clubs acquires nine Wellbridge clubs, expanding to 86 locations across 14 states
health-clubs.context: Genesis Health Clubs announced the acquisition of nine clubs from The Wellbridge Company, including Colorado Athletic Clubs and New Mexico Sports & Wellness properties. The deal expands Genesis to 86 locations across 14 states and marks the operator’s entry into New Mexico. Mid-premium operator consolidation continues as regional platforms absorb independent and smaller-chain footprints.
health-clubs.implication: Post-acquisition equipment refreshes typically occur within 12 to 18 months as new ownership standardizes operations across the combined footprint. Reps should build watch lists against Wellbridge locations now and track Genesis contract anniversaries. The deal also signals that mid-premium M&A activity remains a live channel for refresh pipeline.
health-clubs.conversation: When ownership changes hands, equipment strategy resets. Let me walk you through what post-acquisition refresh cycles typically look like and how we help operators standardize across a combined footprint without disrupting member experience.

health-clubs.headline: Alloy Personal Training takes CapitalSpring investment, targeting franchise expansion beyond 135 US locations
health-clubs.context: Alloy Personal Training, a boutique fitness franchise with 135 locations across 38 states, announced an investment from private equity firm CapitalSpring. The deal provides capital to accelerate franchise unit openings after opening 61 locations in 2025 and 46 in 2024. Each franchise location is independently operated with its own equipment buying authority, not a centrally managed brand.
health-clubs.implication: Franchise growth at this pace means a wave of new-location equipment decisions made by independent owners, not corporate procurement. Reps should engage franchisee networks directly, build referrals from existing Alloy owners in their territory, and position equipment packages designed around the personal training franchise model of small-footprint, high-turnover facilities.
health-clubs.conversation: Alloy just took major investment and is accelerating franchise openings. Each new location is an independent equipment decision, not a corporate rollout. Let me walk you through what equipment packages look like for their franchisee model and how we support new owners through buildout.

health-clubs.headline: Xponential Fitness pays $40M in FTC and franchisee settlements, redirecting capital from 500+ franchisee operators
health-clubs.context: Xponential Fitness agreed to pay nearly $40M in combined FTC and franchisee settlements, including $17M to resolve an FTC investigation and additional compensation to more than 500 current and former franchisees of Club Pilates, Pure Barre, StretchLab, and related boutique brands. The settlement creates a capital redirection event for affected franchisees and a brand-confidence reset across the parent portfolio.
health-clubs.implication: Settlement-funded franchisees face a near-term decision on whether to reinvest in their existing facilities or defer capex. Reps covering Xponential-brand franchisee territories should engage owners directly about equipment refresh plans tied to the settlement capital cycle, and monitor franchise resale activity as some owners exit.
health-clubs.conversation: Your franchisee network just received settlement capital at the same time as brand-level pressure on franchisor relationships. That creates a window for independent equipment conversations that do not rely on corporate approval. Let me walk you through what refresh planning looks like in that context.

hospitality.headline: Houston hotels invest over $100M in renovations and expansions ahead of 2026 FIFA World Cup
hospitality.context: Downtown Houston hotel operators including Marriott, Hilton, and Holiday Inn disclosed over $100M in combined renovation and expansion investment ahead of the June 2026 FIFA World Cup. The JW Marriott Houston Downtown expansion alone adds 56 rooms and new amenity space. Bookings for June-July are up 130% and rates up 300%, driving hotel ownership to accelerate capex ahead of the event window.
hospitality.implication: Event-driven renovation cycles compress decision timelines. Urban hotels refreshing ahead of a fixed deadline cannot afford equipment delivery slippage, which favors vendors with proven service bandwidth. Reps covering Houston-market owners should audit which properties have active PIPs tied to World Cup readiness and lead with installation timeline guarantees, not product spec sheets.
hospitality.conversation: Your refresh cycle has a fixed deadline in June. Let me walk you through our installation timeline guarantees and how we sequence equipment delivery for operators on an event-driven window.

hospitality.headline: Hilton launches Apartment Collection brand, expanding fitness-amenity footprint into extended-stay segment
hospitality.context: Hilton launched Apartment Collection by Hilton in Q1 2026 through partnership with Placemakr, adding approximately 3,000 units to its apartment-style portfolio that sits alongside the existing ~10,000 furnished apartment units. Properties feature on-site fitness centers as standard amenity, extending Hilton’s hospitality fitness footprint into long-stay and corporate relocation markets.
hospitality.implication: The blurring line between hospitality and multi-unit housing creates new hybrid equipment specifications. Extended-stay and apartment-collection properties serve residents for weeks or months, not nights, which drives higher per-unit utilization and different maintenance profiles. Reps should engage hospitality brand teams and multifamily developers equally on this segment.
hospitality.conversation: Your extended-stay properties see utilization patterns closer to multifamily than traditional hospitality. Let me show you equipment specifications designed for that utilization profile and how we support long-term deployment economics.

multi-unit.headline: Greystar launches independent living management platform, extending beyond active adult into senior care
multi-unit.context: Greystar disclosed plans to launch an independent living management platform, extending its senior housing footprint beyond the active adult Overture, Everleigh, and Album brands. The move reflects the operator’s belief that residents increasingly want "convenience, hospitality and light support" as they age, and positions Greystar to capture a larger share of the 28% growth projected in the 80-plus demographic through 2030.
multi-unit.implication: When the largest US multifamily operator extends into independent living, equipment specifications for senior-oriented amenity spaces become a portfolio-level conversation, not a property-by-property decision. Reps covering Greystar should engage the new independent living leadership directly and lead with programming partnership conversations, not product catalog pitches.
multi-unit.conversation: Your independent living platform is building the amenity standard now, before it scales. Let me show you what strength and wellness programming looks like at peer senior housing operators and how we design equipment specifications for aging-in-place residents.

multi-unit.headline: Multifamily architects reframe fitness amenities around flexibility and measurable ROI, not square footage
multi-unit.context: Multifamily Executive published its 2026 amenity trends report with input from architects at Gensler, Hartman Design Group, and KTGY. The consensus: oversized gyms and traditional clubrooms are underperforming, while flexible wellness spaces with movable equipment, spa-zone integration, and measurable engagement outperform. Architects are designing for "ROI-defensible" amenity footprints in a flat-rent environment.
multi-unit.implication: Architects writing specifications now are asking for equipment that supports flexible layouts, usage data, and programming integration. Reps should engage design firms at the spec phase, not the bid phase, and lead with flexibility and data capability over footprint count.
multi-unit.conversation: Your architect is writing specifications for a flat-rent environment, which means flexibility and usage data matter more than size. Let me walk your design team through equipment configurations that support programming changes over a building’s life without renovation.

performance.headline: NFLPA 2026 report cards expose persistent weight room and training facility gaps across the league
performance.context: The NFLPA released its 2026 player report cards in late February, grading all 32 franchises on facilities, staff, and ownership. Multiple franchises received weight room grades of B or below, with specific franchise-level facility gaps called out publicly for the fourth consecutive year. Historical precedent from prior report card cycles shows capex announcements within 6-12 months of low grades, driven by ownership response to player feedback.
performance.implication: Report card grades are a durable capex catalyst across the league and create a predictable 6-12 month pursuit window. Reps covering NFL teams should map franchise grades against facility audit results and engage head S&C coaches ahead of ownership-driven procurement conversations.
performance.conversation: Your franchise’s report card is already public. Ownership is going to ask what the plan is. Let me work with your head strength coach now so the proposal matches the gap the players flagged before the budget conversation gets scheduled.

performance.implication: Conference-level peer pressure around facility spending is a predictable sales catalyst. performance.conversation: Michigan State just committed $1B to its athletic facilities. Your AD is going to field questions about how your program compares. Let me walk you through what a peer-matched S&C facility plan looks like at your scale.

oneBigIdea.headline: Three buyer types, one shortlist. Hospitality, BTR, and elite sport now buy from the same spec.
oneBigIdea.body: Six Senses London opened March 1 with a 2,300m² wellness hub and 325m² fitness centre. Belmond Villa San Michele Florence reopened April 28 after an 18-month Guerlain-spa renovation. Moda’s flagship London BTR at Embassy Boulevard opened with three dedicated fitness spaces — weights, connected-cardio, mind-body — and Fitwel Champion certification across the portfolio. UK Sport named Loughborough, University of Bath, and University of Wolverhampton Elite Training Centres on April 24, anchored by hospitality-grade strength and recovery specs. Three years ago, a five-star hotel, an institutional landlord, and a national sport governing body wrote three different equipment shortlists. Today they write one. Wellness branding crossed hospitality into residential, recovery science crossed elite sport into hospitality, and BTR amenity standards caught both. The same shortlist — weights, cardio, mind-body, recovery, connected-platform integration — now lands on all three buyer desks, and procurement teams cross-reference each other’s installations directly when scoring vendors. Reps carrying cross-vertical proof points — one hotel, one BTR, one university — will out-close siloed reps for the next 12-18 months. After that, buyers institutionalize the cross-reference and the asymmetric advantage closes. The first half of 2026 is when reference accounts get claimed across categories.

oneBigIdea.headline: The single regional pitch is over. Five country playbooks now define the market.
oneBigIdea.body: RIZAP chocoZAP is on track for 2,800 unstaffed gyms by FY3/26 and entering Greater China and Taiwan. Anytime Fitness India is profitable at 180 gyms and targeting 500 over four years. Korea’s fitness market forecasts USD 4.75 billion in 2025 at 9.96% CAGR with AI-enabled smart fitness centres opening in Gangnam. China’s 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) makes sports industry state policy across 4.59 million existing venues. Mandarin Oriental refreshed flagship wellness at Bangkok, Desaru Coast, and The Landmark Hong Kong in six months. Three years ago, one regional pitch covered the territory. That market has fractured. Each country writes its own procurement story now, driven by economics, regulation, technology adoption, and capex priorities. Japan needs staffless durability. India needs profitable franchise economics. Korea needs AI-integration. China needs scale and institutional partnership. Singapore and SEA need luxury references. This is structural, not cyclical. Country-specialist competitors are already winning country-by-country — Japanese-format suppliers in Japan, franchise economics in India, AI-integration in Korea. Reps with country-tailored proof points will out-close single-deck reps through 2026. Territory plans built on one regional reference set will underperform.

The founder decides, and a first-quarter 2027 opening puts the equipment order in the fourth quarter of 2026. A tracked competitor is selling reformers into this recovery and studio format. Put a combined strength and cardio proposal in front of the founder before the studio build-out is final.
health-clubs.conversation: You are giving half of a 12,000-square-foot club to training and opening in early 2027. Let me help you size a 6,000-square-foot strength and cardio floor that leaves room for the recovery zones.

health-clubs.headline: Discover Strength entered Massachusetts with a Wellesley studio and set a target of 250 U.S. studios.
health-clubs.context: Strength-training franchisor Discover Strength will open its first Massachusetts studio at 55 Central St. in Wellesley in early November, Athletech News reported Sept. 24. Local franchisee Alexei Erchak owns the unit and plans more Greater Boston locations. The brand runs 43 studios and targets about 250 in the U.S. Its model uses supervised 30-minute strength sessions twice a week on specialized machines, led by exercise physiologists.
health-clubs.implication: Signal. Growth from 43 to about 250 studios adds more than 200 strength-only floors over the next several years. The Wellesley package is likely ordered for a November opening, so the near-term buyer is the franchisor's development and operations lead, who sets the system equipment specification. Each new Greater Boston unit gives the Northeast rep a second entry point at the franchisee level as sites are signed.
health-clubs.conversation: You are growing from 43 studios toward 250, and your first Boston franchisee is already planning more sites. Let me help you benchmark a compact strength circuit your next studios can open with.

hospitality.headline: Paséa Hotel & Spa owners approved a $17 million renovation that includes the Huntington Beach fitness center.
hospitality.context: The Busch family and Eagle Four Partners, owners of the 250-room Paséa Hotel & Spa in Huntington Beach, California, will spend $17 million on a property-wide renovation, the Orange County Business Journal reported Sept. 28. Scope covers guestrooms, the Aarna Spa, the pool, meeting rooms, the lobby and the fitness center. Pacific Hospitality Group extended its management agreement five years. Guestrooms finish by 2027 and remaining amenities in early 2028.
hospitality.implication: Opportunity. The fitness center sits in the amenity phase that runs into early 2028, so the equipment specification is open. Pacific Hospitality Group operations leadership and the owners' asset manager decide, working with design firm Stylo Haus. Amenity FF&E specifications should lock in 2027, after the guestroom phase. Reach the design team now, while Stylo Haus is still drawing the amenity floors.
hospitality.conversation: Your owners just approved $17 million, and the fitness center is in the 2027 to 2028 amenity phase. Let me help you get a fitness layout in front of Stylo Haus before amenity FF&E is final.

hospitality.headline: Marriott will reflag the 371-room Laguna Cliffs resort in Dana Point as a JW Marriott after a redesign.
hospitality.context: Marriott said Sept. 15 that the 371-room Laguna Cliffs Marriott Resort & Spa in Dana Point, California, will reopen as The Ocean Cliffs at Dana Point, a JW Marriott Resort, after a multimillion-dollar transformation. HKS and ROAM lead a redesign of guestrooms, the lobby, arrival and public spaces, with a new pool, a 6,000-square-foot ballroom and a new restaurant. Aimbridge Hospitality operates. Budget and reopening date were not disclosed.
hospitality.implication: Opportunity. A move from Marriott to JW Marriott brings the brand's higher fitness and well-being standard, so the gym is likely in scope even though the release does not list it. Aimbridge project and procurement leads decide, with HKS and ROAM on design. No reopening date is set, so the specification window likely runs through 2027. Lead with the JW standard, since the owner has to meet it to reopen under the flag.
hospitality.conversation: You are reflagging to JW Marriott, and the brand's well-being standard raises the bar for the gym. Let me help you bring Aimbridge a fitness layout that meets it before HKS locks FF&E.

hospitality.headline: Ink 48 in Manhattan signed as the U.S. flagship for MGallery and will renovate before a 2028 debut.
hospitality.context: Capstone Equities and Leyad signed Ink 48, a 222-room hotel in Manhattan's Hell's Kitchen, as the U.S. flagship for Accor's MGallery Collection, Lodging Magazine reported Sept. 22. The hotel will stay open independently during an extensive renovation that adds MGallery brand elements, with the official debut set for 2028. Rebel Hotel Company will manage after conversion. The property has a fitness center, a rooftop bar and 6,000 square feet of meeting space.
hospitality.implication: Opportunity. A flagship conversion with a 2028 debut gives the owners more than a year to set amenity specifications, and Accor will use the U.S. flagship to show its brand standard. Capstone Equities asset management and development leads decide now, and Rebel Hotel Company operations takes over later. Offer a compact strength and cardio package sized for a boutique footprint. No budget or fitness scope was disclosed.
hospitality.conversation: Ink 48 just signed as the MGallery U.S. flagship and will renovate ahead of a 2028 debut. Let me help you put a boutique-scale fitness package in front of Capstone before specifications close.

multi-unit.headline: Namdar Group closed a $310 million loan for an 873-unit first tower at Journal Square in Jersey City.
multi-unit.context: TYKO provided a $310 million construction loan to Namdar Group for 555 Summit Avenue in Jersey City, the first phase of a two-tower plan totaling 1,542 units, Connect CRE reported Sept. 25. The 47-story first tower will hold 873 studio to two-bedroom units near the Journal Square PATH station. Amenities include a fitness center, rooftop lounge and terrace, club room and coworking space. Newmark arranged the financing.
multi-unit.implication: Opportunity. An 873-unit transit tower needs a fitness center built for peak-hour load, which favors durable, high-throughput equipment. A second tower of 669 units gives Namdar a reason to set one standard across both phases. No completion date is public. Namdar's construction and amenity managers are the buyers, and the supplier that wins phase one holds the inside track on phase two.
multi-unit.conversation: You just closed $310 million to build 873 units at Journal Square, with a second tower behind it. Let me help you set one fitness standard across both phases before the first floor is specified.

multi-unit.headline: Mavrek and Fengate started a 380-unit West Loop tower backed by a $130.4 million construction loan.
multi-unit.context: Affinius Capital provided a $130.4 million construction loan to a Mavrek Development and Fengate Asset Management joint venture for 1000 West Jackson Street in Chicago's West Loop, Commercial Observer reported Sept. 17. The 25-story tower holds 380 units, including 76 affordable units, and 21,500 square feet of retail. Plans include 31,000 square feet of amenities with a pool and a fitness center with a basketball court. Completion is expected mid-2028.
multi-unit.implication: Opportunity. A fitness center paired with a basketball court points to a larger footprint than a typical amenity gym, which suits a full strength and cardio package. A mid-2028 delivery puts equipment specification in 2027 as interiors are finalized. The developer's amenity lead and the interior designer are the buyers to reach now, before the FF&E budget is written. Fengate's institutional backing may bring a portfolio purchasing standard.
multi-unit.conversation: You just started a 25-story, 380-unit West Loop tower with a fitness center and basketball court. Let me help you get an amenity layout in front of the design team before FF&E is set.

multi-unit.headline: Trilogy secured a construction loan for a 172-unit build-to-rent community in Huntsville with a clubhouse gym.
multi-unit.context: Trilogy Investment Co. obtained a construction loan for REV3 at The Celeste, a 172-unit build-to-rent community on Plummer Road in north Huntsville, Alabama, REBusinessOnline reported Sept. 17. The project offers three-bedroom townhomes with attached garages, a resort-style pool, clubhouse, fitness center and outdoor space. Affiliate REV3 Homes is building it as Trilogy's second build-to-rent opportunity zone fund project with Pinnacle Partners. First deliveries are planned for early 2027.
multi-unit.implication: Opportunity. Early 2027 first deliveries put the clubhouse fitness decision inside the next two quarters, the shortest timeline in this vertical. Build-to-rent clubhouse gyms run small and budget-sensitive, so a compact, low-maintenance package fits. Trilogy uses an in-house builder and a fund partnership, which points to a repeatable specification. The owner's development lead and REV3 Homes purchasing decide. Loan amount and lender were not disclosed.
multi-unit.conversation: You are delivering your first Huntsville townhomes in early 2027 with a clubhouse fitness center. Let me help you lock a compact package that REV3 Homes can repeat on your next opportunity zone project.

campus-rec.headline: Alabama trustees authorized planning for an $88 million South Campus recreation center with strength and recovery zones.
campus-rec.context: The University of Alabama Board of Trustees approved a Stage 1 submittal authorizing planning for an $88 million, roughly 75,000-square-foot South Campus Student Recreation Center near Tutwiler Hall, the Tuscaloosa Thread reported Sept. 15. Plans include weight training and cardio areas, functional and hybrid training space, and recovery areas. Barnwell Hall demolition is set for summer 2027. No architect is selected and no construction schedule is set.
campus-rec.implication: Opportunity. A planning-only approval leaves the fitness and recovery plan fully open, and the architect, once hired, will set the floor zoning. University Recreation leadership, UA facilities planning and the design team decide. Construction cost is estimated at just over $65 million, and the project returns to trustees before work begins. Equipment specification likely falls in 2027 or later, so influence on the program brief matters now.
campus-rec.conversation: Your trustees just authorized planning for an $88 million South Campus rec center with strength, cardio and recovery zones. Let me help you build a space-per-student equipment plan before the architect locks the layout.

campus-rec.headline: Williams Baptist broke ground Sept. 22 on a $7 million wellness center with a weight and fitness area.
campus-rec.context: Williams Baptist University in Walnut Ridge, Arkansas, broke ground Sept. 22 on the 26,000-square-foot J.E. and L.E. Mabee Foundation Wellness Center, NEA Report reported. A $4 million Mabee Foundation grant awarded in 2023 anchors the $7 million project. Plans include two basketball courts, pickleball courts, weight and fitness equipment, a student lounge, gaming area and coffee shop. Ramsons Construction of Jonesboro is building it over 18 to 24 months.
campus-rec.implication: Opportunity. A small private campus buying a new wellness center usually purchases one complete cardio, strength and free weight package, through the president's office, the business office and a student life lead. Completion in spring to fall 2028 puts equipment selection in 2027. A turnkey layout and financing offer now can set the specification before other vendors engage. The equipment budget is not disclosed.
campus-rec.conversation: You just broke ground on a $7 million wellness center with a dedicated weight and fitness area. Let me help you plan a turnkey equipment package and layout while the building goes up.

campus-rec.headline: UAH is turning its closed pool into a second weight room with racks, cables and turf.
campus-rec.context: The University of Alabama in Huntsville is converting its pool into a secondary weight room with squat racks, cable machines and a turf training zone, Campus Rec Magazine reported Sept. 10. The project also replaces the roof and windows and updates branding, with completion due by late 2026. UAH closed the pool after reviewing usage data, operating costs and student preferences. No budget was disclosed.
campus-rec.implication: Signal. Completion by late 2026 means the rack, cable and turf package may already be on order, so the near-term move is to confirm status before pitching. The campus recreation director made the pool decision on usage and cost data and owns the buy. If equipment is open, the decision falls this fall. Other campuses with aging, costly pools can follow the same conversion path.
campus-rec.conversation: You are turning your old pool into a second weight room by late 2026. Let me help you confirm whether the strength package is still open and map a rack and cable layout for the space.

military.headline: Fort Benning's H2F Complex targets full operation in January 2027 as the H2F Academy moves to the post.
military.context: The Maneuver Center of Excellence at Fort Benning, Georgia, said its H2F Complex is slated to be fully operational in January 2027, according to H2F director Col. Marcus Wright. Army.mil reported Sept. 22 that the H2F Academy has begun moving to the installation. Senior leaders held a Sept. 16 fitness event at the post's Tactical Athlete Performance Center. The Army cites five to six fewer profile days per musculoskeletal injury under H2F.
military.implication: Opportunity. A January 2027 operational date puts outfitting decisions for the complex in the next one to three months, with contracting officers and the MCoE H2F program office as buyers. The H2F Academy trains strength coaches from across the force, so equipment specified at Benning shapes what coaches expect at other installations. The article names no vendor, and the procurement vehicle is not public.
military.conversation: Your H2F Complex goes fully operational in January 2027, and the H2F Academy is moving in. Let me help you map the contracting contacts and outfitting timeline before the specifications lock.

military.headline: Flint broke ground on a $17 million regional police and fire training center built in four phases.
military.context: Flint, Michigan, broke ground Sept. 10 on a $17 million regional police and fire training center at Stewart and Industrial avenues, Mid-Michigan NOW reported. Plans include a 50-yard indoor range, a future 911 center, a fire training tower and two training rooms, one for virtual simulation. Construction runs in four phases. The fire and police departments each put $250,000 toward design, and the city is still pursuing $3 million in federal funds.
military.implication: Signal. The published plan shows no dedicated fitness space, so this is a design conversation rather than an open equipment order. Fire Chief Theron Wiggins, Police Chief Terence Green and lead architect Adrianna Melchior are the contacts. Phased construction and unsecured federal money push any equipment decision into 2027 or later. A four-phase build leaves room to add a physical readiness room before later phases are drawn.
military.conversation: You are building a $17 million regional training center in four phases. Let me help you make the case for a physical readiness room before the later phases are locked.

performance.headline: Palmyra's school board backed a $72.5 million-plus high school plan with a new gym and fitness facility.
performance.context: The Palmyra Area School Board in Lebanon County, Pennsylvania, backed Option 3 for high school renovations and additions at a Sept. 17 meeting, LebTown reported Sept. 21, with a formal vote set for Oct. 1. The $72.5 million to $84.1 million plan adds a three-station gymnasium with a fitness facility and wrestling space, plus engineering labs and systems upgrades. Superintendent Bernie Kepler said RLPS Architects needs at least a year for designs.
performance.implication: Opportunity. The fitness facility is at the programming stage, so the opening is to get into RLPS Architects' design work before layouts and equipment allowances are set. The athletic director, strength and wrestling coaches and the architect decide, with construction at least a year out. A room shared by physical education classes and athletes favors durable, multi-user selectorized and rack equipment. Size and budget line are not disclosed.
performance.conversation: Your board votes Oct. 1 on a high school plan that adds a fitness facility, and RLPS Architects will design it over the next year. Let me help you get a layout and equipment allowance into the design.

performance.headline: South Dakota began its Gassen Family Fieldhouse build, which frees the DakotaDome for year-round turf.
performance.context: The University of South Dakota announced the groundbreaking for the Gassen Family Fieldhouse on Sept. 24, set to open in summer 2028. The building will house track and field, cross country and triathlon with a 200-meter banked track, throwing cages, student-athlete lounges and a hydrotherapy room, with seating for more than 2,000. The South Dakota Legislature, Bill and Jill Gassen and the late T. Denny Sanford lead the funding.
performance.implication: Signal. USD names no weight room in the fieldhouse, so the building itself buys recovery and training support rather than a full strength floor. The DakotaDome conversion to year-round turf moves training space for other Coyote programs and could reopen the department's strength and conditioning footprint. The athletics director, head strength coach and capital projects staff decide, with outfitting likely in 2027. Cost is not disclosed.
performance.conversation: Your new fieldhouse opens in summer 2028 and frees the DakotaDome for turf. Let me help you plan a strength and recovery package as you move training space across programs.

flags.note: Athletech News reported Sept. 22 that Peloton opened orders for its Commercial Bike and Commercial Tread through its business site. Both carry 23.8-inch rotating touchscreens with live and on-demand classes, and the tread reaches 14 mph at 15 percent incline. Peloton targets gyms, hotels and residential communities. No pricing or customers were disclosed. Peloton now brings its consumer brand into hospitality and multi-unit bids this quarter, backed by Precor service. Counter on heavy-use uptime, years of installed-base data and open content. Give hospitality and multi-unit reps a one-page uptime, warranty and content comparison before the first units ship.

Athletech News reported Sept. 17 that Technogym Reform is on sale in the US in a Sand Stone Collection of wood, Warm Titanium and vegan leather, plus Pearl Grey and Diamond Black. It links to the Technogym app for on-demand workouts. No pricing or US installs were named. Technogym is selling design into the boutique Pilates zone at the luxury hotel and residential accounts where it already sells premium cardio. Counter on breadth across the whole floor and lifetime cost of ownership. Confirm the LF/HS reformer and studio partner options, then brief hospitality reps on answering a request for a Pilates zone.

Athletech News reported Sept. 22 that Playlist launched AI Insights, which benchmarks performance, flags clients likely to churn and forecasts revenue. It went first to Mindbody customers, with the revenue forecast in beta at select US studios. Playlist claims a 19 percent higher rebooking rate among users of its Clients at Risk feature. The article describes no direct EGYM hardware role. Playlist can now pitch booking software, retention data and EGYM hardware to an operator as one package. Counter on an open platform that works with any management system. Document the member-management and booking integrations LF/HS supports and add them to health club proposals.
